newsitem.title: USA: Conn. atty genl urges end to gasoline zone pricing.
newsitem.headline: Conn. atty genl urges end to gasoline zone pricing.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal on Thursday urged state lawmakers to eliminate so-called "zone-pricing," which forces gasoline dealers to buy from certain sources regardless of price.
Blumenthal said in testimony before a legislative committee that eliminating zone pricing would promote lower gasoline prices in the state.
"Supply and demand in Connecticut, not the dictates of oil executives in Texas or California, should determine where and how our gas station owners purchase their product," Blumenthal said.

He said that under current practice, oil companies require gas dealers to purchase gas from certain sources, even though the dealer could have bought the same brand of gas at a lower cost from a different source.
Using "zone pricing," they sell the same gas at different prices to dealers in different areas of the state, he said.

"Instead of the present practice, permitting big oil corporations to establish minimum gallon purchase requirements which result in less competition among gasoline dealers, the market should govern how many gallons of gasoline a dealer must sell in order to be competeitive in the Connecticut market," Blumenthal said.
